#826. NWSL playoff predictions: who can spoil Gotham’s bid for the double?

Our panel breaks down the players to watch, the dark horses, the state of the league and the top candidates to reach the championship game in DC

Compelling storylines that kept the league interesting during a crowded sports summer. The interval years that aren’t Olympic or World Cup years are often quieter for the NWSL (see: average attendance was essentially flat among the non-expansion teams). In a year with the men’s World Cup on home soil and a major anniversary season for the WNBA, most of the NWSL’s teams gave a solid showing, with close competition for the Shield, an entertaining Golden Boot race and the returns of several big stars. Even those teams who did not give a solid showing – hello, Chicago – finally made some encouraging moves in the right direction. (Louisville next, please.) Ella Brockway

The league working to gauge the heart of its fanbase. Recent weeks have seen contentious scenes, especially in Portland, as transphobic organizations try to work into the league discourse as they have with the WNBA. But beyond that, there have been considerable innovations made with an eye on garnering more attention. The “Rodman Rule” was hurried to production in part to keep arguably the most marketable US player from going abroad. The league briefly considered following MLS’s lead and inverting its schedule, only for a vote to be spurned after initial backlash from players and the public. It even got a feature in Ted Lasso. These efforts take time, but that’s a lot of willingness to change just about anything about the league’s structure if it moves the needle. Jeff Rueter

Races to the top – and the bottom. The competition for both the Shield and Golden Boot was fierce. Ashley Sanchez pulled ahead for the Boot, but Barbra Banda, Sophia Wilson, Janine Sonis and Trinity Rodman provided some real fireworks. (Had Banda not been kept out of the country for the last month of games due to federal travel policies, she may have given Sanchez a run for her money.) The Shield race was even tighter, with three teams still in contention with two matches to go. However, the league struggled to maintain that quality across the board. Chicago, Louisville and Bay FC were embarrassingly bad – and boring – throughout the season. It’s a story that is too familiar, and doesn’t seem poised to change in a real way any time soon. As much as the league’s marketing centers parity, its choices prioritize expansion. With two new clubs arriving in 2028 and more on the way after, I worry the talent across the board will continue to be watered down, especially as the league’s salary cap and low minimum salary drives elite players away to teams in Europe, Mexico and Brazil. The NWSL will have to contend with what growing pains are inevitable, and which should really be avoided. Abigail Segel

Denver Summit. I’m as disappointed as anyone that we won’t get to see Sanchez’s goalscoring feats continue this postseason, but I’d also like to see what Denver and their goalscorers could have done as just the second expansion franchise to reach the playoffs in their first year. They tied 2018 North Carolina with the third-most goals (53) of a team in any regular season. EB

On talent and in moments, it felt like expansion Denver Summit’s place in the top eight would be inevitable. Ultimately, inconsistency and an inability to turn close games from draws into wins held them back. Only Chicago had a more languid defensive press after the summer break, and while being the league’s lowest-fouling team wins spirit points, it did afford Denver’s opponents plenty of time to build into sequences. JR

For the second year in a row, the North Carolina Courage. The Courage spent most of the season above the playoff line, but when Sanchez’s numbers came back down to earth in the final month, they lacked an attacking structure to keep the goalscoring, which had papered over their leaky defense all year. Mak Lind will look to use his first full offseason to find a sustainable way to make up for Manaka Matsukubo’s absence – her midseason departure to Chelsea did him no favors, and the success they had for almost the entire rest of the season is all the more impressive considering it. AS

Angel City. No team is in better form. After a rough start to the season, Angel City steadied the ship after the summer break and have been blistering of late, with eight wins, two draws and zero losses since 31 August. They have nine goals in their last three, and will have new signing Maddie DiMaria, fresh off a 12-goal showing at the U-17 World Cup, available to face Kansas City. I’d fear them. EB

For once, Gotham don’t qualify. Since selling Alyssa Thompson to Chelsea, Angel City have come out of their doldrums with impressive aptitude. No team has maintained a higher points-per-game rate since 28 August (2.6), and they notched a draw at Gotham and an away win over Washington. Ally Sentnor has made a quick acclimation, and there’s considerable talent including Sveindís Jónsdóttir’s goal threat, Emily Sams’s defensive mettle and Gisele Thompson’s all-around strengths. JR

Angel City. The club whose branding has traditionally been better than its soccer started the season hot, but within a few games they fell back to their expected place in the middle of the table. In June, GM Mark Parsons had seen enough, and gave the boot to manager Alexander Straus. His interim replacement, Leif Smerud, has managed to get the most out of the roster by bringing them back to the basics. Even Sentnor, who did not reach her potential at Utah or Kansas City, has been shining bright after joining midseason. This is a scrappy team peaking at the right time. AS

I know the danger of picking against this team in the playoffs, but I’ll say Gotham. Of any team in this league, they are probably the one with the best plug-and-play system, where players can fill in for others as needed. The question: will they have the healthy bodies to do so? Much depends on the availability of Jaelin Howell, Rose Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw. EB

I wouldn’t say I necessarily expect any of the top four to falter, but seeding isn’t the only reason I’d lean Kansas City. For a few years now, the Current have been able to outlast the fiercest of challenges thanks to the singular brilliance of Temwa Chawinga on the break, but Angel City’s Sarah Gorden is the rare defender with the backtracking pace to keep in stride with the Malawi international. The Current fare well against teams trying to play out of the back, but Angel City are quite capable at bunkering and countering. I could see them pulling a quick curtain on Chris Armas’s first NWSL postseason. JR

Washington had their best performance of the season on 17 October, defeating rival Gotham for the first time since 2024. It was finally a complete, convincing game from an inconsistent side. But the following game, at Kansas City, was a 2-1 loss made significantly worse by midfield mainstay Hal Hershfelt tearing her ACL. Next was Decision Day against last-place Chicago. Instead of a rout, the Spirit put in a quiet 2-0 win that left little confidence the team is peaking for the playoffs. Washington have reached the last two finals, and it’s possible they will again, but they need to quickly solidify a midfield that’s been fluid all season and will rely heavily on new players Clara Luvanga and Mélissa Bethi to perform as if they know the league inside and out. AS

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Trinity Rodman. For the first time in two years – I almost want to knock on wood as I’m typing – the Washington Spirit’s star forward enters the NWSL postseason healthy. In 2024, she played every minute of their three playoff games but was battling back issues throughout. In 2025, she was limited to just 35 minutes in three games with an MCL injury. This year, she started all 30 regular-season games and played some of her best soccer (12 goals and eight assists). She’s vital to any Spirit run. EB

If you haven’t yet had the pleasure, make sure to watch Pietra Tordin. The Portland Thorns playmaker has been electric in her second season, settling in as a tricky attacking midfielder with plenty of tricks to thwart anyone marking her one-v-one. Her partnership with Wilson will keep Washington from getting too comfortable, and she’s absolutely one to watch for the USWNT in the short and long term after debuting for Emma Hayes in October. JR

The Current have perhaps the most exciting roster of attackers in the league. Chawinga, Michelle Cooper, Debinha and Haley Hopkins are a formidable bunch. Yet the mastermind behind them is who makes everything tick. Croix Bethune remains the most fun player to watch in the league, constantly connecting teammates and creating chances out of thin air. Bethune was out with an injury earlier this fall but has come back without missing a beat, including earning an assist against her former Washington team two weeks ago. If Bethune continues her MVP-caliber season, there’s nothing Kansas City can’t do. AS

San Diego 2-1 Angel City. An all-west coast matchup for an east coast final. Angel City have a win and a draw with Kansas City this season (albeit the latter result was against a shorthanded Current team). They’re good at pulling off surprises, and I can see a run to the final in DC. The Wave fell just short of the Shield, but they’ve done an excellent job assembling talent across the experience range, from rookie-of-the-year favorite Mimi Van Zanten to 23-year-old Trinity Byars to Kenza Dali, a sneaky MVP candidate at 35. They have the blend to take home the championship. EB

Gotham 2-1 San Diego. While high-flying attacks win hearts and minds, a dependable defense is an invaluable floor-raiser. Gotham won their first Shield thanks to establishing greater control in matches, but their low goalscoring record suggests there’s more to tap into in the final third. I back the collective brilliance of Lavelle, Shaw and Sam Kerr to step up as they so often do in the big moments. JR

San Diego 2-1 Angel City. The bracket feels awfully lopsided this year. The winner of Kansas City v Angel City will probably face off against Gotham in New Jersey for the semi-finals (assuming the Shield winners defeat eighth-place Seattle). Gotham are postseason monsters, as evidenced in 2023 and 2025, but without the injured Howell and Jordynn Dudley, they look a lot less sturdy and a lot less threatening. (Keeper Ann-Katrin Berger, however, can negate a multitude of sins.) The winner of this semi-final is a toss-up between the three, but I’ll go with Angel City for the sake of chaos. On the other side of the bracket, San Diego are peaking while Washington, Portland and Utah are much less convincing. The Wave have nearly perfected their possession-based style with an extremely balanced and consistent lineup. I don’t see a better team right now. AS

#825. Dolly Parton's Estate Drops Lawsuit Against Her Nephew Bryan Seaver

More than a month after Dolly Parton's estate She's Alive LLC filed a lawsuit against her nephew Bryan Seaver, the company run by her longtime manager Danny Nozell requested to dismiss the case.

Dolly Parton's estate is clocking out of the family drama.

More than a month after nephew Bryan Seaver was hit with a lawsuit from She's Alive LLC—a company run by Dolly's longtime manager Danny Nozell, established to protect her businesses after her August death—the organization filed to dismiss the suit, according to court documents obtained by The New York Times and People.

The Nov. 5 notice of voluntary dismissal with the Chancery Court of Tennessee was filed without prejudice, so her estate could refile if it chooses.

Following the dismissal filing, Seaver's attorney Dominic J. Leonardo emphasized that his client's love for Parton—who tapped her nephew to announce her death at age 80—was there each step of the way.

"Mr. Seaver cares deeply about his Aunt Dolly, her music, her family, and the incredible legacy she left behind," he said in a statement to TMZ. "He has made a career out of protecting his aunt while she was alive and remains committed to Dolly and his entire family."

"Mr. Seaver is grateful to put this misunderstanding behind him," the message continued, "so that the entire family can continue to grieve peacefully and ensure that the bright light of Dolly's legacy remains entirely untouched."

E! News has reached out to Leonardo for comment and has not yet heard back.

Seaver—who was fired from his longtime role shortly before the lawsuit and an additional temporary restraining order was filed and granted—was accused of embarking on an "obscene, deliberate, and escalating campaign of threats" before and after Parton's death to get money from her estate, according to the September lawsuit obtained by E! News.

In one alleged instance detailed in the suit, her former head of security threatened to ruin a Dollywood business relationship. The message purportedly read, "I'm going to destroy the entire brand if you don't get these [Dollywood business partners] out of our bit."

Another exchange allegedly sent after the "Jolene" singer's death appeared to show Seaver threatening to start a podcast "dedicated to ruining Dolly's brand partnerships and telling the violations" people "have done on us."

"It's going to be great," Seaver purportedly wrote to Nozell. "Or f--king pay me."

Meanwhile, the temporary restraining order was granted, in which he was barred from contacting and coming within 1,000 feet of She's Alive employees and business partners, as well as entering company properties or interfering with business relationships

In response to the request made by She's Alive to extend the restraining order in October, Seaver vehemently denied the accusations against him, though he acknowledged using harsh language in his interactions.

"They were sent in the course of private conversations between two friends," he argued in the October affidavit obtained by CBS News, "who were both frustrated, grieving, and discussing strategy following Ms. Parton's illness and death."

He alleged the messages were not threats but rather a "private warning” about potential associates wanting to harm Parton's brand.

"I have declined to speak with the media about this case and have asked my attorneys to handle all media communications," Seaver concluded in the doc. "I care about Ms. Parton, her music, her legacy, and her family. I do not want this dispute to harm her legacy."

#824. Golden Bachelorette’s Joan Vassos, Chock Chapple Break Up

Golden Bachelorette stars Joan Vassos and Chock Chappel have broken up, calling off their engagement two years after they met on the inaugural season of the Bachelor Nation franchise.

Joan Vassos and Chock Chapple, who met on the inaugural season of The Golden Bachelorette have broken up, calling off their engagement after two years together.

"Two years ago, Chock and I took a leap of faith and got engaged during our season of The Golden Bachelorette, hoping we had found our forever," a statement shared to Vassos' Instagram Stories Nov. 6 read. "We spent the last two years living what we hoped would be the beginning of our love story, sharing our families, amazing adventures, laughter and supporting each other through challenging times."

However, as she and Chapple—who also shared the same statement to his account—noted, "Sadly, our journey hasn't turned out the way we had hoped and we have decided to end our engagement."

"We truly want each other to be happy," she concluded, "and I'm grateful for the chapter we shared."

Vassos first raised eyebrows about her and Chapple’s relationship status when she stepped out at the Page Six Virtual Reali-Tea Awards Oct. 6 without her engagement ring.

Following Chapple’s proposal to Vassos in the July 2024 finale of The Golden Bachelorette, the couple had a slow and steady approach to planning their nuptials, previously teasing they’d be open to a televised ceremony like The Golden Bachelor’s Gerry Turner and Theresa Nist opted for. (The inaugural Golden couple split just two months later.)

“As far as televised or just like a little private thing, [we] originally thought private—just our friends and family, smaller, maybe destination,” Vassos told E! News in 2024. “But now, we’re thinking maybe we’d be open for a televised one.”

Still, the former school administrator expressed hesitation.

“Bachelor Nation has kind of watched us through this whole journey,” she reasoned, “and then to abruptly end it and not show anybody the next chapter of it would be not really that kind. And so we’re thinking about maybe, maybe doing that.”

At the time, Vassos and Chapple, both 63, expressed hope to walk down the aisle “within a year” but also had more pressing hopes for their then-budding relationship.

“We’re just happy to not have anything epic to do right now because that’s all we’ve been doing for the last six months,” Vassos explained, noting they were looking forward to the opportunity to “be a couple and enjoy each other and get to know each other’s friends and family.”

For the couple, that also meant exploring the possibility of moving to New York together.

“We’re just excited,” Chapple told E! “I think it’s going to be fun to watch Joan handle all this—from the furnishings to everything else to where we live. We get along so well I’m like, 'This is yours. It was my gift to you. You pick it. You pick exactly what you want.’”

In the final episode of The Golden Bachelorette, Chapple had beat out runner-up Guy Gansert in winning Vassos’ heart in his Bora Bora proposal.

"I still think I'm in a dream and I'm just going to wake up,” Chapple told Vassos in the finale. “But Joan, I love you and I want you to be in my life.”

Vassos, for her part, had eagerly accepted Chapple’s hand.

“You made me feel comfortable, you made me feel safe, I felt like we could take care of each other,” she told him, “and I knew you would never hurt me.”

#823. Fifa wants talks over restricting women’s Olympic football to under-23s

IOC open to dialogue and Fifa wants input from others

Fifa concerned about fixture congestion and workload

Fifa wants talks with the International Olympic Committee over restricting the Olympic women’s football tournament to under-23s owing to concerns over fixture congestion and the workload of senior players.

The eligibility criteria for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles has been set, with qualification tournaments having begun in some regions, so no change can be made until Brisbane 2032 at the earliest, but sources at both organisations have said that they are open to dialogue.

Although no formal proposal has been made, Fifa is understood to be interested in examining the matter in talks with the IOC and other key stakeholders, such as the players and leading member associations whose national sides routinely qualify for the Games.

A move to bring in age restrictions would dramatically alter the nature of the event and require careful analysis, consultation and consideration through Fifa and IOC processes.

Such a change would be controversial and could provoke a backlash from leading international players because the Olympics has long been regarded as one of the highlights of the women’s calendar, with Emma Hayes’s United States team securing gold in Paris two years ago. The Olympic title has been contested eight times and the US have won five.

Women’s football also has a major commercial appeal for the IOC, particularly in markets such as the US, Europe and Australia, so it may resist Fifa’s overtures.

Women’s football was introduced to the Olympics at Atlanta in 1996, and as an amateur sport at that time never had eligibility requirements, in contrast to the men’s game.

After admitting football to the Olympic programme in 1908 the IOC did not permit professionals to take part until 1984 owing to Fifa’s insistence on maintaining the primacy of the World Cup, as well as the demands on players from a congested calendar. Under pressure from Fifa the IOC introduced an under-23 age restriction in 1992, although three overage players have also been allowed in each squad since 1996.

The huge growth and professionalisation of the women’s game over the past decade has created increased fixture congestion, with the 2028 calendar the most bloated yet.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Fifa is to a large extent culpable for this because the world governing body has chosen to launch the Women’s Club World Cup in an Olympic year, with the US to stage the 16-team competition between 5 and 30 January, six months before the Games.

The Women’s Club World Cup will cause major disruption to the European club season, with Arsenal and Chelsea or Manchester City likely to be absent from domestic competition for up to a month if they reach the latter stages, missing four Women’s Super League matches and the FA Cup fourth round. The importance of the sport to the IOC is shown by the fact that the women’s football tournament will be bigger than the men’s for the first time in LA, featuring 16 teams to 12, in a reversal of the numbers at Paris 2024.

#822. Jalen Brunson’s Law & Order: SVU Debut Is Anything But Heinous

NBA star Jalen Brunson turned over an epic performance on the Nov. 5 episode of Law & Order: SVU, working alongside New York Knicks superfan Mariska Hargitay.

Just when it thought Jalen Brunson’s 2026 couldn’t get any better—having already clinched an NBA Championship title, a finals MVP award and an SNL hosting gig—he can also now add detective to his resume.

The New York Knicks point guard just assisted his good pal and Knicks superfan Mariska Hargitay with a guest appearance on the Nov. 5 episode of Law & Order: SVU.

In the scene, Hargitay’s Olivia Benson meets up with Brunson’s character in a restaurant, remarking, “Detective Madison. Look at you out of uniform, huh? Congratulations on the promotion.”

Brunson (a.k.a. Detective Madison) is seated at the counter dressed in nondescript clothing, save for the NYPD badge hanging around his neck.

“Thanks, Captain,” the detective, whose name is a cheeky hat-tip to the Knicks home stadium Madison Square Garden, responds. “Focused on my goals, gave it 110 percent. Things worked out.”

And in what is perhaps a veiled nod to the Knicks’ epic victory—during which Brunson was a key player who, in fact, did give it 110 percent—Benson responds with a small smile, “Yeah, they did.”

From there, the scene involves Det. Madison giving Benson the rundown on a former perp he got tangled with, calling him a “real pain in the ass.” Her interest is especially piqued, however, by his mention of a metal rod in the vehicle.

The info turns out to be a slam dunk, with the metal rod later confirmed as the weapon the episode’s victim had been attacked with, serving as the evidence the team needed to hopefully put the perp away for good.

And while Brunson’s cameo was nothing more than a fast break in the action of the episode, his presence still packed a punch.

“Short appearance but I loved it,” one fan wrote on Law & Order’s Instagram post teasing his appearance, while another added, “Jalen is so very talented!!!”

Brunson and Hargitay’s onscreen appearance was a perfect full-circle moment for fans, who have long loved seeing the Law & Order actress sitting courtside in MSG to cheer on Brunson and the team.

In fact, Brunson has gone so far as to even say Hargitay gets top billing on his personal Mt. Rushmore of celebrity Knicks fans.

“My number one, love her to death, and she knows it—Mariska Hargitay,” Brunson previously revealed to Richard Jefferson, who pointed out the Knicks player was blushing as he said it.

Thankfully, the feeling is very mutual, with Hargitay saying she feels “profoundly grateful” for Brunson’s leadership on the Knicks and how the team has “brought our city together.”

#821. Was Dr. Seuss Even a Doctor? Secrets About The Cat in the Hat Revealed

The reimagined Cat in the Hat starring Bill Hader officially hits theaters Nov. 6. Take a look to learn everything about Dr. Seuss, the man who wrote the original book.

You couldn’t call Theodor Seuss Geisel a fool, but one thing is true: He did not go to medical school.

The children’s book author, better known as Dr. Seuss, created a world of whimsy that has inspired countless movies and TV shows—including The Cat in the Hat, in theaters today, Nov. 6. But despite his famous title, Seuss never actually earned a doctorate.

In fact, while Seuss briefly attended Oxford to pursue a PhD, he dropped out according to Dr. Seuss & Mr. Geisel: A Biography, to focus on writing.

Instead, he adopted the pen name to honor his father, who always wanted him to be a doctor. Of course, after using the title for years, he finally earned it when his alma mater Dartmouth College awarded him an honorary doctorate in 1956.

As for how Cat in the Hat came to be? Seuss had written several books before he started teaching kids it was fun to have fun. In the 1950s, a director at Houghton Mifflin—a youth technology and reading company—challenged him to write a book using a list of children’s words without sounding absurd.

And so, The Cat in the Hat was born using just over 200 words most used by kids and created a world so vivid you could see it behind your eyelids.

But before there was the cat in the hat, Seuss—who died in 1991 at age 87—considered other animals to be his star. Ultimately, he settled on feline because they're self-assured and rebellious—and perhaps because “Dog in a Log” and “Mouse in a Blouse” don’t have quite the same ring to it.

From there, however, the cat’s origin story stops. The author deliberately made the mischievous character's backstory a mystery, allowing readers to imagine something on their own.

Since hitting shelves, The Cat in the Hat has been sold millions of copies, introducing generations of young readers to the joy of rhyme. It also, of course, has earned the Hollywood fix. Mike Myers brought the character alive in the 2003 live-action alongside Dakota Fanning and Alec Baldwin. And now Bill Hader is lending his voice to the character in the latest flick.

#819. Africa's first Youth Olympics open in Senegal amid hope and scrutiny

Senegal is hosting Africa's first Youth Olympics, with 2,700 young athletes competing in Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. The Games bring pride and hope, but also questions over cost, rights and legacy.

On the final day of October, what may well be the final Summer Youth Olympics ever will begin. It will be the first on African soil as around 2,700 athletes aged 15-17 arrive in Senegal to compete across a total of 153 events in 25 sports.

Hosted in eight venues across three locations – Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly, 80 kilometers (50 miles) from the capital – these Games are seen by many as a prelude to Africa hosting a full Olympics one day in the future.

"I'm really excited about the Youth Olympic Games because, for the first time, I'll be representing our country," 15-year-old judoka Aisha Diop who is competing for Senegal told DW.

"I am very proud to be able to represent my country at these Games. This will really motivate young African athletes because they will improve, and they will want to continue playing sports now that the Youth Games have been held here."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The 2026 Youth Games in Senegal will also be a first beyond the history it is making in Africa.

"Of the 2,700 athletes who will be competing in Dakar, there will be a 50-50 split between men and women," Olivia Nloga, Chief Brand Promotion Officer on the organizing committee, told DW.

"But this parity isn't just reflected in the overall figure. This gender parity will also be reflected in each event and in each sport where such parity actually exists."

Several sports are also making their debut at the Youth Olympic Games, such as five-a-side baseball, kung fu and the Senegalese specialty of beach wrestling. There's also a refugee team at the Youth Olympic Games for the first time.

"As I said earlier, the Youth Olympic Games aren't just about sports, and they aren't just about infrastructure," said Nloga.

"For us, it was also important to use this time to build on and reinforce the idea that these Games in Senegal are a celebration for the people. We did this by investing in culture—for example, through a fashion show and a program called Yi-sol, which is a mural project on the city's walls."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Other projects designed to celebrate the people include music, and a local student designed the mascot. The biggest focus of all though, is on creating sustainability for the young people of Senegal.

"We did so through a program that is very important to us – one that is close to our hearts, namely, the Olympic Civic and Sports Certificate," Nloga said.

"We traveled to schools throughout Senegal and worked with more than 1,000 instructors to reach and make an impact on more than one million young Senegalese children who, during this hiatus, were exposed to and educated about the values of the Olympic Movement."

With recent flooding in the country, there were concerns that infrastructure would have been affected, but Nloga insisted that flood risk had long been in the planning.

"The prime minister held an interdepartmental meeting during which he established a task force to ensure that the necessary arrangements and follow-up measures are put in place to safeguard both the competition venues and the accommodation sites."

With Formula 1 confirming its return to Africa earlier in October, global sport is slowly becoming a more regular event in Africa. As a result though, there have been questions asked about the legacy of such events.

Many in Senegal concerned by the high cost of living and unemployment will see these Games as an unnecessary expense. For the Senegalese authorities though, they are an opportunity for long-term investment in the country's young people as well as infrastructure. There is also the hope that this will make Dakar a major tourist destination.

There was further criticism of the Games being in Senegal from Human Rights Watch (HRW), with the NGO calling on the Senegalese authorities to change their stance on the LGBTQ+ community.

"You are welcoming all of the world. It shouldn't be 'you are welcome to our country, except this, except that,'" Larissa Kojoue from HRW told DW.

"Anti-LGBT legislation and that crackdown that is going on, they contradict the Olympic movement, the Olympic Charter, and also various human rights convention that the country has signed."

Earlier this year, Senegal President Bassirou Diomaye Faye signed into law new legislation on same-sex relations that have proved contentious abroad despite broad political support within the majority Muslim country's parliament. Several human rights groups had voiced concerns about the bill, including warning that it would dissuade people at risk of illnesses like HIV/AIDS from seeking help.

The Games were set to see the return of Russians to Olympic competition under their own colours after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) lifted their suspension in July.

However, the Russian Athletics Federation (RusAF) released a statement the day before the opening ceremony saying the reported 13 athletes (and 10 coaches) had been exluded from the competition. They demanded an explanation and asked for the decision to be reconsidered.

"The IOC-endorsed position was clear in its direction: young athletes holding Russian or Belarusian passports should no longer be restricted from international youth competitions. That principle should apply to Dakar 2026," read the statement.

Despite the IOC's ruling, each federation can still decide whether to authorize Russian participation. World Athletics, has clearly upheld their ban, while swimming and judo have allowed Russian athletes back.

"This has enabled World Athletics to pursue its own exclusory agenda in the face of clear and just directions from the IOC. This activism is only detrimental to youth sports, with the result being that Russian young athletes will be denied the opportunity to compete at these Games."

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Despite the various concerns, there is an overriding hope that the Games will be prove beneficial for all involved.

"What makes the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar special is that they are also rooted in Senegal's extremely strong sporting culture," Nloga said.

"Every evening, when you take a stroll along the Corniche in Dakar, you're struck by the number of people you see exercising, regardless of their age or physical condition. What we'll be offering during these Olympic Games is also an immersion into Senegalese life – into the way sports are just as much a part of Senegalese identity."

This article was updated on October 30, 2026 to reflect the change in situation for Russian athletes at the Games.

Sira Thierij conducted interviews for this article. Edited by: Chuck Penfold

#818. Kamada’s late leveller rescues point for 10-man Crystal Palace and denies Hoffenheim

A late, late strike from Daichi Kamada saved Crystal Palace from embarrassment and another round of navel gazing as they snatched a Europa League draw with Hoffenheim against the odds.

After being outplayed by a side currently in the bottom half of the Bundesliga, and a goal down from the seventh minute, Palace looked to have lost all hope in this fixture when Adam Wharton was dismissed with 13 minutes to go. But after Hoffenheim failed to clear a goalmouth scramble in added time, Kamada fired home under the keeper to generate a rare moment of elation at Selhurst Park this season.

After the match, the beleaguered Pierre Sage struggled to put a positive gloss on events. Asked if he thought his team had deserved their point, he said it “depended on the moment of the game”, and while he had praise for his side’s attitude he was critical of their tactical performance. “Offensively we did better than our two previous games but we have to continue to improve defensively”, he said. “We gave up too much space to the opponent and sometimes we had difficulty in duels. When we try to attack a little bit we are very quickly open.”

To be fair to Sage, this was an accurate call. Palace were in the match throughout without ever dominating, and Hoffenheim created the best chances in the game without ever having to try too hard. Sitting in 20th place in the Europa League, Palace have work to do in this competition, offering no respite from their Premier League travails as they prepare for a visit from Liverpool on Sunday.

With a tea-time kick-off on Bonfire Night, a family-friendly crowd might have had a right to expect fireworks. Palace set off with intensity but were sloppy too and coughed up an easy opening goal in the game’s early knockings. Wharton gave possession away cheaply about 20 yards from the Hoffenheim goal. There were perhaps just three touches before the ball reached Tim Lemperle wide right, who whipped the ball first time to the advancing Alexander Prass. The winger’s shot was equally immediate and caught Dean Henderson cold, his save too slow, and the ball squirmed through his midriff before rolling over the line.

The Palace support did not moan and got on with backing their side. Sadly the team on the pitch did not respond in desired fashion and Hoffenheim should have scored again through a Andrej Kramaric volley in the 23rd minute, well saved by Henderson on this occasion, before Palace started to work their way into the game.

Malick Yalcouyé scored his fourth goal of the season to break the deadlock in a hard-fought encounter in Madrid.

The Seagulls are now the only team not to have conceded a goal in the competition so far and their seven points from three matches leaves them fifth in the table.

“It’s what we expected,” said Hürzeler. “These games in the Conference League are different. You have to beat the low block. We didn’t play our best game, to be fair. But in the end we kept a clean sheet – the fifth clean sheet in a row in this tournament – and then we scored the goal and I think we deserved to win this game.”

The Swiss side Lugano are top of the Conference League, with maximum points after a 3-0 win over Kauno Zalgiris at the AIL Arena.

Panathinaikos beat CSKA Sofia 2-1 to also make it three straight wins, Twente beat 10-man Pafos 3-1 and Monaco saw off Nordsjælland 2-0 to extend their own 100% start.

Ajax ran out 6-1 winners away to 10-man Midtjylland, while a depleted Hearts side lost 3-1 away to Thun in Switzerland.

Yéremy Pino was the focus of the home side’s hopes and he was both Palace’s brightest spark and their greatest frustration. He could find the gaps that no one else could but his delivery was either inaccurate or overcomplicated.

He did at least find the right weight on a through ball to Kamada on the half hour, only for his fellow No 10 in Sage’s system to pull a cross-shot beyond Oliver Baumann’s far post. Hoffenheim had a better opportunity for themselves just before half-time, Ozan Kabak heading over at a corner when unmarked six yards out.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

The second half began with another burst of intensity from Palace but it fizzled out again and within 10 minutes Sage had made a double change, pulling Kamada back into midfield and bringing Eddie Nketiah into the front three to strengthen Palace’s finishing options. In the 66th minute Palace created their best chance of the match, when Wharton feigned to shoot from the edge of the box, cut left and slipped in Pino, who looked to shoot over the advancing Baumann only for the keeper to stand his ground and deflect the ball to safety.

You might have thought a rally could spring from there, but no. Hoffenheim soon won a couple of corners on the bounce and killed any momentum for the home side.

Then Wharton got himself sent off, making a poor decision to lead with his elbow in contesting a header. Horatiu Fesnic did not need a second look and despite Wharton’s protestations the referee showed him a second yellow card.

A sense of injustice did at least succeed in inducing some pep into Palace’s performance while Hoffenheim stepped back and sought to run down the clock. Palace created only one opportunity and that was a bit of a mess, but if there was to be respite from their perilous Premier League condition it was going to need a bit of fortune, and Kamada duly seized upon it when it arrived.

Martha Stewart is serving up some more accountability for her actions.

Though she emphasized that she usually does very "elaborate costumes," she said she "didn't have a costume" because Melvin—who was dressed as her BFF Snoop Dogg for Today's beloved Halloween episode—dropped chocolate ganache on her white sweater as they learned to decorate a themed cheesecake.

At the time, the FBI confirmed its involvement in the investigation into Thomas, noting it would “provide support, as appropriate, to the Philippine authorities. We will also investigate any related allegations of federal violations of U.S. law.”

As for Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex—who shares two children with husband Prince Harry—shared she was “deeply distressed” over the allegations in a statement with E! News, noting her thoughts were with “any children who may have been harmed.”

The 45-year-old also shared insight into what information she’d been made privy to previously.

“In 2018, a letter was sent to the Metropolitan Police and Royalty and Specialist Protection,” she explained. “That letter was subsequently shared with me. It made troubling and disturbing allegations against my father and I was given assurances that these were being investigated.”

Though she didn’t specify he allegations, she noted they’re a large reason she’s been estranged from Thomas in recent years.

“I hope it can now be understood that despite certain media publications' distortion over the years,” she said, “any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children, was for one reason: to protect them.”

As for now, she hopes justice can be served.

“The breadth of what has now been uncovered is more sickening than one could ever imagine,” Meghan concluded. “The priority remains the safety and protection of innocent children.”

(E! and MS NOW are both part of Versant Media family.)

#814. America Ferrera Reveals What She Knows About Barbie 2

As the deal for the sequel to Greta Gerwig’s Barbie movie up in the air, star America Ferrera revealed what she knows about the film in an exclusive E! News interview for The Cat in the Hat.

America Ferrera is a Barbie girl, but she knows nothing about the Barbie 2 world.

While the sequel for Greta Gerwig’s film inspired by the Mattel toy and starring Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling has been up in the air for years, Ferrera admitted that she’s just Ken, er, Gloria—and doesn’t have any update.

“I don’t know anything about Barbie 2,” Ferrera admitted in an exclusive E! News interview for The Cat in the Hat alongside costar Paula Pell. “I don’t have to pretend like I don’t know anything because I actually don’t know anything.”

Ferrera’s update comes as speculation swirls around the possibility for a follow-up to the 2023 film, with reports earlier this year noting that the movie could be shelved due to ongoing salary negotiations between Warner Bros. and the original film’s cast.

Meanwhile, Ferrera—mom to Sebastian, 8, and Lucia, 6, with husband Ryan Piers Williams—is excited about bringing another iconic character to life, starring as mom Carmen in the Bill Hader-led film.

“The Cat in the Hat is so iconic,” the Ugly Betty alum mused. “I grew up loving Dr. Seuss books and I have two littles and I’ve read The Cat in the Hat to them a ton. Actually, my favorite part of the book was always the very last line of the book which was, ‘What would you do if your mother asked you?’ And I’d always turn to my kids and be like, ‘Would you tell me the truth?’”

Fast forward to this opportunity, Ferrera admitted it felt as easy as counting one fish, two fish, red fish, blue fish to take the role.

“Getting to say to my kids I’m going to be the voice of the mom in The Cat in the Hat, I did it for them,” she mused. “But a little bit for me.”

And Ferrera’s kids already gave her a glowing review for the film, also starring Quinta Brunson and Bowen Yang, which officially hits theaters today, Nov. 6.

“We saw it yesterday,” she revealed. “We had the best time. They loved it. It was really sweet.”

Of course, Ferrera isn’t so sure her kids would, in fact, tell her if The Cat in the Hat came for a visit.

“I can’t tell if it gave me cool mom points or if they’re like, ‘Ugh, mom that’s you,’” she joked. “Because I am such a mom in this, too, where they were like, ‘We’ve heard the same things.’”

While Barbie 2 still remains uncertain, keep reading for secrets about the original film…

Margot Robbie, who stars as Barbie and also produced the film, admitted that she always wanted Ryan Gosling to be her Ken. She said he was written into the script—as the character "Ken Ryan Gosling"—and joked, "We pretty much wouldn't take no for an answer."

Writer-director Greta Gerwig had her back too. "We just kept bothering you," she said to to Ryan in an SXM interview. "Margot was like, 'Is it weird if I go to his house?' I was like, 'Don't go to his house. We're just gonna stay put.' Send a follow-up text."

As Margot teased, "I would see a sea of blue on my phone."

Margot gave Ryan daily gifts inspired by his character Beach Ken.

"She left a pink present with a pink bow, from Barbie to Ken, every day while we were filming," Ryan told Vogue. "They were all beach-related. Like puka shells, or a sign that says 'Pray for surf.'"

He said that he's "never quite figured out" what Ken's job as "Beach" means, "But I felt like she was trying to help Ken understand, through these gifts that she was giving."

"I think we said it was scheduling conflict, that's what we said," Amy Schumer said on Watch What Happens Live With Andy Cohen in June 2023. "But yeah, it really was just, like, creative differences. But you know what? There's, like, a new team behind it, and it looks like it's very feminist and cool. So, I will be seeing that movie."

These Barbies were almost movie stars—or, rather, these movie stars were almost Barbies. After Amy left the movie, Anne Hathaway was signed up to take the lead, but it was later reported that she was no longer involved. When Margot got on board, she tried to recruit Gal Gadot to join as another Barbie, but the Wonder Woman star wasn't available.

Greta's former Lady Bird and Little Women muse Saoirse Ronan was also set to appear in the film but had to cancel. "I was supposed to do a cameo because I live in London and they were [filming] there," the actress admitted to People. "There was a whole character I was going to play—another Barbie. I was gutted I couldn't do it."

"We've always tried to get in a proper fart joke and we've never done it," Greta told IndieWire. "We had like a fart opera in the middle [of Barbie]. I thought it was really funny... And that was not the consensus."

But her editor Nick Houy has hope she'll let one rip in a future film: "We need to work it into a more significant narrative moment next time."

While the script comedically name-drops other shows and movies—like the The Godfather, Pride and Prejudice and Zack Snyder's Justice League—there are multiple Easter eggs to The Wizard of Oz hidden in the set. A movie theater marquee shows that the 1939 film is playing in the doll world, but the inspiration didn't stop there.

"[The Wizard of Oz] does something that I wanted to emulate," Greta said in an interview, "which it's using these incredible sound stages and these painted skies and this sense of 'authentic artificial,' which I think is very beautiful and emotional."

The 39-year-old explained, "I think of the painted backdrop of the Emerald City as they go towards it, and we put in our movie, we have the pink brick road, instead of the yellow brick road. We also have beautiful painted backdrops of horizons. We executed it like they would have done in the ‘30s and ‘40s."

Spreading Christmas cheer in July, Will Ferrell made some cheeky nods to his beloved Elf character Buddy while playing the Mattel CEO in the Barbie movie.

Among the discreet references to the 2003 comedy? He demands to be the one to press a button in the Mattel office elevator (calling back to the Elf scene where he presses every button in his dad's office building elevator, because the lights look "like a Christmas tree").

In Barbie, his suited character also starts a tickle fight—just like Buddy the Elf does with his dad Walter (James Caan) while being tucked into bed one night.

Going where no Barbie has gone before... The opening scene of Barbie pays homage to the 1968 Stanley Kubrick film 2001: A Space Odyssey, which shows a group of hominins discovering a futuristic monolith. In Barbie, a group of girls are shocked by a giant version of the original 1959 Barbie doll, wearing a black and white striped swimsuit.

Fans speculate that Gloria's daughter Sasha (Ariana Greenblatt) and her friends in the cafeteria were inspired by Barbie's rivals, the original Bratz dolls: Sasha, Chloe, Yasmin and Jade.

Casting director Allison Jones revealed Saturday Night Live star Bowen Yang, Schitt's Creek actor Dan Levy and Dear Evan Hansen actor Ben Platt almost played Kens in the movie but weren't able to make it work. She added, "They were, I'm not kidding, really bummed they couldn't do it."

According to the casting director, before Michael Cera came on board as Ken's buddy Allan, the part almost went to a certain Frozen actor.

"Dear, dear Jonathan Groff was like, 'I can't believe I'm typing this,'" Allison told Vanity Fair, "'but I can't do Allan.'"

America Ferrera's IRL husband Ryan Piers Williams plays none other than her character Gloria's husband. Ryan—whose past work includes producing, writing and acting in X/Y with America in 2014—is credited as "El Esposo de Gloria."

"It was a happy accident," John Cena told Today of his casting as a Mermaid Ken. He said he "kind of" pitched himself to join the film "in an accidental run-in with Margot Robbie."

As he recalled, he told the actress, "'I would do, pretty much, whatever you guys need 'cause I really enjoy the movie,' and they asked me if I wanted to be a merman."

The French version of Barbie's poster went viral after social media users pointed out the double entendre of the translation. The tagline, "She can do everything. He's just Ken," was translated to, "Elle peut tout faire. Lui, c'est juste Ken."

However, fans went wild after pointing out that "ken" has a slang meaning in French as "f--k" and would translate to, "He can only f--k." Bonjour, Ken!

The Barbie actresses had a cast sleepover at London hotel Claridge's to get close. "We all shared beds and wore our pajamas, and ordered room service," Margot revealed on The Kelly Clarkson Show, "and played games, and found out that America is exceptionally competitive."

America had her own tea to spill about the evening. "Nobody told me that it was a sexy Barbie sleepover," she quipped. "So everybody was in like really pretty silky nightgowns, and I was in like the most grandma floral twin set you can imagine."

As for the Kens? "Greta was very deliberate in what she wanted the Kens to do to bond," Simu Liu exclusively told E! News, "which was to gym together."

Though Nicola Coughlan only appeared for a few moments in the film, it was very important to her that she experience life in plastic.

"I auditioned for Barbie back in January '22 when I was on holiday with friends," she wrote on Instagram. "I'd packed one random hot pink dress I hadn't worn at all and when I had to make my audition tape I thought—this is fate, I have a dress in Barbie Pink!"

Admitting she's "obsessed" with Greta, the Bridgerton star said that "the prospect of working with her was something I couldn't even have imagined."

"When I found out she wanted to have me be part of @barbiethemovie, and then that I probably wouldn't be able to make it work because of my schedule I was firstly elated and quickly heartbroken," Nicola continued. "So when I was asked if I wanted to pop into Barbieland even briefly my answer was an immediate, and very emphatic yes."

The film concludes with Margot adopting a new life as a human named Barbara Handler, a reference to Barbie inventor Ruth Handler's real-life daughter. Barbie enters an office building and delivers her final line to a receptionist: "I'm here to see my gynecologist."

Why did Greta end on that note? "With this film, it was important for me that everything operated on at least two levels," she told USA Today. "I knew I wanted to end on a mic drop kind of joke, but I also find it very emotional. When I was a teenage girl, I remember growing up and being embarrassed about my body, and just feeling ashamed in a way that I couldn't even describe. It felt like everything had to be hidden."

The director hoped the way Margot delivered the line with a "big old smile on her face" and with "such happiness and joy" would help de-stigmatize conversations about women's health and "give girls that feeling of, 'Barbie does it, too'—that's both funny and emotional."

#813. Scott Parker’s dramatic West Ham return leaves him struggling for words

The former midfielder with impressive managerial promotion record began with a thrilling comeback in draw at Cardiff

Three days in and Scott Parker has already lost his voice. West Ham’s head coach arrived on Tuesday, watched his side fight back from 3-0 down to draw with Cardiff on Wednesday and was struggling to make himself heard when he met the media on Thursday afternoon.

“It’s like in the summer holidays,” Parker said. “You put the flip-flops on for five weeks, then you come back home and you get your shoes on. You’re in a minute, you’ve got a blister on the back of your heel. It’s the same with a throat. I’ve not shouted for a little while. All of a sudden there’s shouting and it’s a bit croaky.”

Parker is back in the thick of it. Out of work after leaving Burnley in the wake of relegation from the Premier League last April, he cut short his break from management when West Ham parted company with Nuno Espírito Santo. Nuno was sacked early on Tuesday and replaced by Parker, who is intent on leading West Ham out of the Championship at the first time of asking.

It will not be easy. West Ham occupy the final playoff spot after three games without a win and displayed their inconsistencies against Cardiff. They made another slow start, conceding three during the first half, but roared back after a triple half-time change from Parker. Jarrod Bowen was inspired. But Parker needs complete performances if West Ham are to win automatic promotion.

“The Championship’s a tough league,” he said. “It doesn’t matter what name you have on a bit of paper. You have to have a level of humility of what this league needs. That’s a challenge when you come out of the Premier League.”

Parker argued that talent was not enough. Burnley were stingy when they won promotion. Parker has to sort out West Ham’s defence. “Of course we want to play a certain brand,” the 46-year-old said. “But I think it’s just a non-negotiable in terms of a committed team.”

Connections need to be rebuilt with disillusioned supporters. Parker was an all-action midfielder who loved his four years at West Ham as a player. He has added Mark Noble to his backroom staff. Noble has held the role of West Ham’s sporting director since retiring in 2022 but Parker confirmed the former club captain would have a role as an assistant coach. “He’s going to be coaching with me and be that sounding board,” Parker said.

Noble will be able to get Parker up to speed on his squad. West Ham need improvement at the back, better balance in midfield and more bite up front. Nils Koppen, the director of recruitment, could be busy in January. Parker wants to give everyone a clean slate, though. Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Álvarez will have opportunities. Even Maxwel Cornet travelled with the squad to Cardiff.

Parker did not focus during negotiations with Karim Virani, West Ham’s interim CEO, and Daniel Kretinsky, the club’s largest shareholder, on whether funds would be available for signings. One step at a time.

West Ham are in transition. David Sullivan still owns a 40% stake but is no longer on the board. Kretinsky’s power has grown, although the Czech billionaire is yet to say much in public. Parker has heard more from Kretinsky than most people.

“I found a man that was hugely passionate,” Parker said. “I instantly felt that, along with Karim, along with Nils. These were three people who know where they want the club to go.”

The target is a return to the top flight. Parker has won promotion with Bournemouth, Burnley and Fulham but his record at keeping teams up is less impressive. He has been dismissed a little unfairly as nothing more than a promotion specialist.

“In a short space of a coaching career I’ve had some huge success,” Parker said. “I’ve had some blips in terms of two full seasons in the Premier League. All I know is that I’m fully committed.”

That mindset convinced Kretinsky, Virani and Koppen to pick Parker. They wanted his knowledge of the club and record at this level.

West Ham are eighth before visiting Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. They are taking 7,000 fans to Ewood Park and Parker knows there can be no more complacency.
